title: Norm-preserving lifts for a Tate epimorphism surjective on canonical reductions
statement:
Let $K$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field], complete for a nontrivial real-valued nonarchimedean absolute value. A Tate algebra $T_r=K\langle X_1,\ldots,X_rangle$ is the restricted-series ring of [def-trf-restricted-series-presentation], with Gauss norm $\|\sum a_
u X^
u\|_G=\sup_
u|a_
u|$. Let $C
e0$ be a reduced quotient of such an algebra with its affinoid Banach topology. Define $ho(c)=\sup_\chi|\chi(c)|$, where $\chi:C	o K$ runs over continuous unital $K$-algebra homomorphisms. Put $V=\{a:|a|\le1\}$, $\mathfrak m=\{a:|a|<1\}$, $\kappa=V/\mathfrak m$, and $\widetilde C=\{c:ho(c)\le1\}/\{c:ho(c)<1\}$. Let $q:T_s	o C$ be a specified continuous surjective $K$-algebra homomorphism, for $s\ge0$, such that $ho(q(f))\le\|f\|_G$ for all $f\in T_s$. Suppose the $\kappa$-algebra map $\kappa[X_1,\ldots,X_s]	o\widetilde C$ sending $X_i$ to the class of $q(X_i)$ is surjective. Then for every $c\in C$ there is $f\in T_s$ such that $q(f)=c$ and $\|f\|_G=ho(c)$.

source.place: BGR sections 6.4.2–6.4.3, the epimorphism/reduction criterion over a stable field with spectral values in the base value group, together with Corollary 5.2.7/8 (attainment of the Tate quotient norm). Algebraically closed complete base-field specialization. Exact criterion numbering has not been verified because the book is absent. Rodriguez Vazquez, Non-Archimedean normal families, section 2.2, printed pp.1685–1686, verifies the norm-preserving lifting conclusion for distinguished epimorphisms, read online 2026-10-24. Archival copy WANTED; not present in this checkout.

proof.text: Put $R=V\langle X_1,\ldots,X_s\rangle=\{f:\|f\|_G\le1\}$ and $S=\{c:\rho(c)\le1\}$. By [lem-trf-affinoid-spectral-banach-norm], the given $\rho$ is a complete nonarchimedean $K$-algebra norm. The function $\rho_{T_s}$ defined, as for $C$, by continuous characters equals the Gauss norm, so $\{\rho_{T_s}\le1\}=R$. Indeed every $K$-algebra map $\chi:T_s\to K$ satisfies $|\chi(f)|\le\|f\|_G$ for $f$ with constant coefficient $c_0$: otherwise $\lambda=\chi(f)$ has $|\lambda|>\|f\|_G\ge|c_0|$, so $f-\lambda$ has constant coefficient $c_0-\lambda$ of absolute value $|\lambda|>\|f-c_0\|_G$, and [lem-trf-tate-unit-coefficient-criterion] makes $f-\lambda$ a unit with $\chi(f-\lambda)=0$, impossible. Hence every character is continuous, and the continuous characters are exactly the quotient maps $T_s\to T_s/\mathfrak n$ for maximal ideals $\mathfrak n$, whose residue fields are finite over $K$ by [lem-trf-affinoid-supremum-seminorm-calculus], hence equal to $K$ with its own absolute value as $K$ is algebraically closed. So $\rho_{T_s}$ is the maximal-ideal supremum of that node, which on a Tate algebra equals the Gauss norm. Apply [lem-trf-finite-affinoid-unit-ball-finiteness] to $A=T_s$, $B=C$ and $\varphi=q$. Both algebras are nonzero and the target $C$ is reduced, $q$ is continuous and spectrally contractive by hypothesis, and $C$ is cyclic as a $T_s$-module: $c=q(f)\cdot1$. Consequently $S$ is a finite $R$-module. The image $q(R)$ is an $R$-submodule of $S$.

proof.text: The value group $|K^\times|$ is dense in $\mathbf R_{>0}$. Indeed choose $b$ with $0<|b|<1$ by nontriviality and inversion; algebraic closedness supplies all roots of $b$, so the group contains $|b|^{\mathbf Q}$, dense by density of $\mathbf Q$ after taking logarithms. By the scalar and sum inequalities of [lem-trf-affinoid-spectral-banach-norm], $\mathfrak m S=\{c:\rho(c)<1\}$: each finite sum of products $a_jc_j$ with $|a_j|<1$, $\rho(c_j)\le1$ has norm less than one. Conversely for $\rho(c)<1$ choose $a\in K^\times$ with $\rho(c)<|a|<1$; then $c=a(a^{-1}c)$ with $a\in\mathfrak m$ and $a^{-1}c\in S$. Thus $\widetilde C=S/\mathfrak m S$.

source.place: Agent assembly from finite maps on spectral unit balls (6.4.1, verified online via Conrad Lecture 12 p.2), Nakayama (Stacks 00DV, lemma-NAK), and best approximation (5.2.7/8, local book WANTED). No reliance on an unverified 6.4.3 reduction criterion.

proof.text: For $c\in S$, the reduction hypothesis supplies a polynomial $\bar P\in\kappa[X_1,\ldots,X_s]$ representing its class. Lift its finitely many coefficients to $V$ to obtain $P\in R$. The difference $c-q(P)$ lies in $\{\rho<1\}=\mathfrak m S$ by step 2. Therefore $S=q(R)+\mathfrak m S$. Set $Q=S/q(R)$ and let $J=\mathfrak m R$ be the ideal generated in $R$ by the scalar elements of $\mathfrak m$. The images in $Q$ of the finite generators from step 1 generate $Q$, and the displayed equality gives $JQ=Q$.

source.place: Agent assembly from finite maps on spectral unit balls (6.4.1, verified online via Conrad Lecture 12 p.2), Nakayama (Stacks 00DV, lemma-NAK), and best approximation (5.2.7/8, local book WANTED). No reliance on an unverified 6.4.3 reduction criterion.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-one-plus-ideal-annihilator] over $R$ with $I=J$ and $M=Q$. It gives $h=1+i$ with $i\in J$ and $hQ=0$. Write $i=\sum_{j=1}^n a_jr_j$, with $a_j\in\mathfrak m$ and $r_j\in R$. The Gauss inequalities in [lem-trf-restricted-series-gauss-completion] give $\|i\|_G\le\max_j|a_j|<1$ (the empty sum is zero). The constant coefficient of $h$ has absolute value one and its nonconstant part has Gauss norm less than one. Hence [lem-trf-tate-unit-coefficient-criterion] gives an inverse $g\in T_s$. From $g=1-ig$ the same Gauss inequalities give $\|g\|_G\le\max(1,\|i\|_G\|g\|_G)$, which forces $\|g\|_G\le1$. Thus $g\in R$, $h$ is a unit in $R$, and $hQ=0$ implies $Q=0$. We have proved $q(R)=S$.

proof.text: Fix $c\in C$. Choose $f_0\in T_s$ with $q(f_0)=c$. Apply [lem-trf-tate-ideal-best-approximation] to the ideal $I=\ker q$ and $f_0$. It gives a representative $f$ of $f_0+I$ of minimum Gauss norm among all representatives, hence $q(f)=c$. Contractivity gives $\rho(c)\le\|f\|_G$. If the inequality were strict, density from step 2 would supply $a\in K^\times$ with $\rho(c)<|a|<\|f\|_G$. The scalar rule in [lem-trf-affinoid-spectral-banach-norm] gives $a^{-1}c\in S$. By step 4 choose $r\in R$ with $q(r)=a^{-1}c$. Then $q(ar)=c$ and, directly by scaling the coefficients, $\|ar\|_G=|a|\|r\|_G\le|a|<\|f\|_G$, contradicting minimality. Thus $\|f\|_G=\rho(c)$. For $c=0$ one can also take $f=0$; all arguments include $s=0$.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q111-78126d204 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, both new nodes and all seven cited statements in full. The statement is unchanged and exact: an algebraically closed complete field K, a reduced C≠0, a specified contractive q, and a surjective reduction map give lifts f with ‖f‖_G=ρ(c). This is the converse direction of BGR's distinguished-epimorphism criterion. BGR, Conrad L12 and Werner are absent locally: the worker marked them WANTED and set proof_origin to agent. I checked the mathematics independently. Steps 2–5 are correct. Step 2: the value group is dense, and mS={ρ<1}. Step 3: S=q(R)+mS, and Q=S/q(R) is finite with JQ=Q. Step 4: Nakayama gives h=1+i; h is a unit in T_s by the coefficient criterion, and ‖h⁻¹‖≤1, so Q=0. Step 5: best approximation for ker q, then a scaling contradiction. The edge cases c=0 and s=0 are covered. Repair (C4) in step 1: the step identified the unit ball of T_s, defined by continuous characters, with R by citing the supremum-seminorm-calculus node, whose ρ is a supremum over maximal ideals. Every maximal-ideal character being continuous, which this needs, was not argued. The fix adds a three-line argument and adds lem-trf-tate-unit-coefficient-criterion to the step's uses (it was already in proof_deps). The argument: |χ(f)|>‖f‖_G would make f−χ(f) a unit in ker χ, so every character is contractive, and continuous characters are exactly the maximal-ideal quotients with residue field K. New nodes: unit-ball-finiteness is true; reducedness of the target is needed (K→K[ε]/ε² fails), and contractivity is automatic. It is not a duplicate: grauert-remmert-powerbounded reaches the item (I verified the cycle), and the integral-equation nodes give only integrality. Best-approximation is BGR 5.2.7/8, strict closedness of the ideals of T_n. It is not covered by the ℓ-adic finite-dimensional best-approximation node or by the quotient-norm-topology node. Neither node restates the item. No cycle, no SGA, no tool_uses; the searches cover all three kinds.
